purpose: Change apply_version_plan (crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs) so that when multiple plan.bumps'/plan.rewrites' Manifest-trait-routed writes (VersionWriteTarget::Manifest / DepWriteTarget::Manifest) target the same physical manifest path, that path's manifest handle is opened once, mutated once per entry destined for it (bump before rewrites, rewrites in plan.rewrites order), and persisted exactly once -- collapsing what today is N independent open+parse+mutate+persist(atomic_write: temp file + rename + fsync parent + fsync grandparent) cycles into 1. A path that also receives a WorkspaceCargoResolver-routed write to the same root_manifest (VersionWriteTarget::CargoWorkspacePackage or DepWriteTarget::CargoWorkspaceDependency) is excluded from batching entirely via a full pre-scan of plan.bumps and plan.rewrites performed before any mutation begins, and continues to use today's unbatched per-entry immediate open/mutate/persist behavior.
scope: crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs: apply_version_plan's existing bumps loop and rewrites loop are restructured into (1) a pre-scan/classification pass over plan.bumps and plan.rewrites that partitions Manifest-trait-routed write targets into batchable groups (keyed by path) and a mixed-routing exclusion set (paths also named by a WorkspaceCargoResolver-routed root_manifest), (2) a batched-write pass that opens each batchable path once, applies its bump mutation (if any, subject to today's skip/write/error version-precondition check against handle.current_version() -- see ManifestWriteGroup in api_surface, which replicates apply.rs:83-96's three-way branch exactly) then its rewrite mutations in plan.rewrites order, and persists exactly once but only when at least one mutation (the bump's write_version, or any rewrite's update_dependency_spec) actually occurred in memory, and (3) preservation of today's unbatched per-entry open/mutate/persist code path for every Manifest-trait entry whose path is in the exclusion set. A new private/pub(crate) classification function (see api_surface) is added to apply.rs, independently unit-testable from apply_version_plan. The VersionWriteTarget::CargoWorkspacePackage and DepWriteTarget::CargoWorkspaceDependency arms (WorkspaceCargoResolver call sites) are untouched -- they keep calling ws_res.write_version/write_dependency immediately, per entry, exactly as today. crates/callisto-manifests/src/lib.rs: a new persist-call-count instrumentation pair (persist_call_count/reset_persist_call_count), analogous to the existing open_call_count/reset_open_call_count (lib.rs:108-124), backed by its own process-global AtomicUsize distinct from OPEN_CALL_COUNT. crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs, npm.rs, python.rs: each type's persist() implementation (CargoToml::persist, PackageJson::persist, PyprojectToml::persist -- introduced by SPEC-MANIFEST-PERSIST-001) increments the new counter by one immediately after its underlying atomic_write call returns Ok; a persist call that returns Err (e.g. the atomic_write failure path exercised by SPEC-MANIFEST-PERSIST-001's AC-011/AC-011b) does NOT increment the counter. crates/callisto-graph/tests/apply_persist_open_count_test.rs: extended with persist_call_count assertions alongside the existing open_call_count assertions, plus a new #[serial] test in the same file for the mixed-routing exclusion regression (a workspace root Cargo.toml with TWO plain, non-inherited dependencies and one workspace-inherited dependency, all three rewritten in the same plan -- the two-plain-dependency shape is mandatory per AC-005, because a single plain entry yields open_call_count() == 1 whether or not the exclusion guard works). crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs's own #[cfg(test)] module: new tests for the classification function in isolation (done independent of apply_version_plan), for rewrite-to-rewrite iteration order on one shared path (two same-RewriteKey SpecRewrite entries with different `to` values, per AC-011; bump-before-rewrites is deliberately not byte-tested -- see AC-017, which grounds that sequencing in AC-014 and AC-016 instead), for the multi-entry-per-file byte-correctness fixture, and for the partial-failure-mid-batch behavior change. WorkspaceCargoResolver's own internal write_version/write_dependency/persist implementation in crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs is NOT modified by this spec beyond the persist-counter instrumentation named above, which does not apply to it (WorkspaceCargoResolver never implements the Manifest trait and is not part of the counted persist() calls -- see non_goals).
non_goals: Reordering apply_version_plan so WorkspaceCargoResolver writes always execute before a mixed path's batched Manifest group. Considered and explicitly rejected in favor of the simpler batching-exclusion approach, to keep this spec's risk profile low after the original combined spec's data-loss ordering bug forced a split into Spec A (SPEC-MANIFEST-PERSIST-001) and this deferred spec.

Extending the Spec A mutate/persist split pattern to WorkspaceCargoResolver itself, or adding persist-call-count instrumentation to WorkspaceCargoResolver::persist. WorkspaceCargoResolver-routed writes (VersionWriteTarget::CargoWorkspacePackage, DepWriteTarget::CargoWorkspaceDependency) remain immediate, per-entry, combined mutate+persist, exactly as before this spec, for both batched-eligible and mixed-routing paths.
plan.changelog_writes, plan.consumed_changesets, plan.pre_state_update/delete_pre_json, and lockfile refresh logic in apply.rs -- untouched, same exclusion boundary as Spec A.

Any change to how cascade.rs (crates/callisto-graph/src/cascade.rs) routes edges between DepWriteTarget::Manifest and DepWriteTarget::CargoWorkspaceDependency. That routing and its correctness is locked in by SPEC-MANIFEST-PERSIST-001's AC-017 regression test and is a precondition this spec relies on, not something it changes.

Adding a production constructor for VersionWriteTarget::CargoWorkspacePackage. It remains dead/unconstructed in production code paths; this spec's mixed-routing exclusion guard covers it defensively (it is a live, constructible enum variant reachable from hand-built VersionPlan values and from tests) without making it reachable from any real planner output.

Defining batching or exclusion behavior for a VersionPlan where two or more distinct PlannedBump entries' writes both target the same manifest path via VersionWriteTarget::Manifest. The requirement's own language ('the path's bump mutation, if any') presumes at most one bump targets a given canonical manifest path per apply_version_plan call, consistent with each package having exactly one canonical manifest and with SPEC-MANIFEST-PERSIST-001's AC-017 precedent of relying on (rather than re-verifying) upstream planner invariants. No evidence in the source requirement or in cascade.rs indicates this scenario is planner-constructible; this spec does not add a runtime check for it and its behavior (if hand-constructed by a test or a future caller) is left unspecified rather than given an invented, untested resolution. This exclusion also covers the narrower case of a single PlannedBump's own `writes: Vec<VersionWriteTarget>` containing two or more VersionWriteTarget::Manifest entries at the identical path -- harmless in practice (classify_manifest_writes would simply record the same (bump_index, target_version) pair, since every VersionWriteTarget::Manifest entry within one PlannedBump shares that bump's single `to` value, so re-recording it a second time for the same path is idempotent) but likewise left without a dedicated test by this spec, for the same 'not planner-constructible, not worth an invented resolution' reasoning.

Any change to Manifest::persist's error type, error mapping, or the atomic_write failure semantics defined in crates/callisto-model/src/atomic.rs. Persist-call-count instrumentation only counts completed successful persists; it does not change what persist() returns or when it fails.

Retrying, resuming, or rolling forward a plan whose batched write for one path failed partway through. The all-or-nothing-per-file behavior change (see AC-004, AC-012, and AC-014) only specifies what apply_version_plan itself leaves on disk and what error it returns; recovery/retry orchestration for the caller is out of scope, unchanged from today.

api_surface.name: apply_version_plan
api_surface.signature: fn apply_version_plan<R: CommandRunner>(root: &Path, plan: &VersionPlan, runner: &R, opts: &ApplyOptions, permit: &ApplyPermit) -> Result<ApplyOutcome, GraphError>
api_surface.description:
Public signature is unchanged by this spec -- no parameter, return type, or error type is added, removed, or reordered. Only the internal bumps-loop/rewrites-loop implementation changes: the current 'for bump { for write { open; mutate; persist } }' and 'for rewrite { open; mutate; persist }' shape is replaced by a pre-scan/classify pass followed by a batched-write pass (for non-mixed paths) and the existing unbatched per-entry pass (for mixed paths and for all CargoWorkspacePackage/CargoWorkspaceDependency arms, which are untouched).

The batched-write pass processes groups strictly sequentially: one path's group is fully opened, mutated, and either persisted or errored-out before the next group's handle is ever opened. No implementation may hold two groups' handles open concurrently, and no implementation may hoist all groups' opens ahead of a shared mutate/persist loop as an optimization. This matters concretely, not just as a general caution: CargoToml::update_dependency_spec's inherited-dependency delegation block (crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs:303-315, within the function's full span at cargo.rs:288-375) delegates a workspace-inherited dependency's rewrite to WorkspaceCargoResolver::write_dependency, which loads, writes, and persists the ROOT Cargo.toml as a side effect from inside a batched group's own rewrite step (this only occurs for DepWriteTarget::Manifest entries whose kind maps to an inherited_deps-tracked name -- SPEC-MANIFEST-PERSIST-001's AC-017 establishes that real cascade.rs-produced plans never route an inherited dependency through DepWriteTarget::Manifest in the first place, so this path-within-a-path only matters for hand-constructed test plans, but this spec's own AC-005-style fixtures deliberately exercise the adjacent CargoWorkspaceDependency case and must not be allowed to interact with a concurrently-open batched handle). Strict group-at-a-time sequencing is also the property AC-012 already depends on for its P1-before-P2 ordering proof; it is stated here as an explicit implementation constraint on apply_version_plan itself, not left implied by a single acceptance criterion.

ApplyOutcome.staged's contents and ordering CHANGE from today's actual behavior, and this spec explicitly decides the new contract rather than leaving it unspecified. TODAY (pre-Spec-B, verified against the current code): modified_paths.push(p.clone()) runs unconditionally once per Manifest-trait entry (apply.rs:97 in the bumps loop, apply.rs:122 in the rewrites loop), with NO deduplication; outcome.staged = modified_paths is assigned directly (apply.rs:335); the only contains()-guarded dedup in the function applies to the separate lockfile-staging loop (apply.rs:294), not to Manifest-trait entries. So today, N Manifest-trait entries sharing one path P produce P appearing in staged N times, and staged's ordering follows plan-encounter order (all bumps-loop entries in plan.bumps/writes order, then all rewrites-loop entries in plan.rewrites order). This description is NOT 'unchanged' as a prior draft of this spec incorrectly claimed -- 'one entry per distinct modified path, in the same relative order paths were first encountered' describes neither today's real behavior nor an unmodified carry-forward.

AFTER this spec: a batched group contributes exactly ONE entry to modified_paths/staged for its path, regardless of how many bump/rewrite entries were folded into that group -- a deliberate, documented behavior change in the same category as AC-004's all-or-nothing persist semantics, verified by AC-018. Ordering for batched paths is NOT guaranteed to match plan-encounter order, because classify_manifest_writes's `batched: BTreeMap<PathBuf, ManifestWriteGroup>` iterates in lexicographic PathBuf order rather than plan-encounter order; this spec does not pin any specific relative ordering between batched-pass-staged paths, unbatched/mixed-routing-pass-staged paths, and changelog/changeset/pre.json paths. This is stated as an explicit, deliberate non-guarantee rather than left as a silent, unstated assumption -- no known caller depends on staged's ordering (the `git add --`/`git rm --cached` calls built from `existing`/`deleted` groupings at apply.rs:300-333 are order-insensitive to the paths passed as CLI arguments).

api_surface.name: classify_manifest_writes
api_surface.description: New pub(crate) function added to crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs, called once at the start of apply_version_plan before any manifest is opened or mutated. Performs the full pre-scan required by the requirement: (1) collects every VersionWriteTarget::CargoWorkspacePackage{root_manifest} from plan.bumps and every DepWriteTarget::CargoWorkspaceDependency{root_manifest} from plan.rewrites into a resolver-routed path set; (2) collects every VersionWriteTarget::Manifest(p) from plan.bumps (recording the owning PlannedBump's index and target version) and every DepWriteTarget::Manifest(p) from plan.rewrites (recording the SpecRewrite in plan.rewrites order) into a manifest-routed-by-path map; (3) partitions that map into `batched: BTreeMap<PathBuf, ManifestWriteGroup>` (paths NOT present in the resolver-routed path set) and `excluded: BTreeSet<PathBuf>` (paths present in both). Path comparison is plain PathBuf equality over the same relative-to-root PathBuf values already used throughout apply.rs (e.g. the values pushed into modified_paths) -- no filesystem canonicalization is performed. This equality check is safe, not merely assumed: production code only ever constructs a VersionWriteTarget::CargoWorkspacePackage/DepWriteTarget::CargoWorkspaceDependency root_manifest value as the literal PathBuf::from("Cargo.toml") -- the same normalized value ManifestDecl::new produces for the workspace root's own canonical manifest path -- so a root-manifest bump and a root-manifest inherited-dependency rewrite are always recognized as the same path; see AC-015 for the cited, falsifiable proof of this cross-module invariant. Returns a ManifestWriteClassification { batched: BTreeMap<PathBuf, ManifestWriteGroup>, excluded: BTreeSet<PathBuf> } value. This function performs no I/O (it reads only the in-memory VersionPlan) and cannot fail -- it has no Result return type.

api_surface.name: ManifestWriteGroup
api_surface.signature: struct ManifestWriteGroup { bump: Option<(usize, Version)>, rewrite_indices: Vec<usize> }
api_surface.description: New pub(crate) struct in apply.rs, produced by classify_manifest_writes for each batchable path. `bump` is Some((bump_index_in_plan_bumps, target_version)) when exactly one PlannedBump's writes target this path via VersionWriteTarget::Manifest; `rewrite_indices` lists, in plan.rewrites order, the indices of every SpecRewrite whose DepWriteTarget::Manifest names this path. The batched-write pass, for each group, opens the path's manifest handle once via callisto_manifests::open, then performs the bump step BEFORE any rewrite is applied, replicating today's three-way precondition branch at apply.rs:83-96 exactly rather than unconditionally calling write_version: if `bump` is Some((bump_idx, target_version)), it reads handle.current_version()?; if current == target_version, the bump mutation is skipped entirely -- no call to handle.write_version, no mutation performed, and an in-memory `mutated` flag stays false -- and the pass proceeds directly to rewrites; if current == plan.bumps[bump_idx].from, handle.write_version(target_version, permit)? is called (mutating in memory) and `mutated` is set true, then the pass proceeds to rewrites; otherwise apply_version_plan returns Err(GraphError::UnexpectedManifestVersion { path, expected_from, expected_to, found }) immediately -- no rewrite in rewrite_indices is applied and handle.persist is never called for this group (see AC-014). If `bump` is None, the bump step performs no precondition check at all (mirroring today's rewrites-loop, which has none of its own) and `mutated` starts false. After the bump step completes without an early return, the pass iterates rewrite_indices in plan.rewrites order, calling handle.update_dependency_spec(...) for each and setting `mutated = true` after each successful call (a no-op re-assignment if `mutated` was already true from the bump step); if any rewrite mutation errors, apply_version_plan returns that error immediately and handle.persist is never called for this group (see AC-004). Only after BOTH the bump step AND the full rewrite_indices iteration have completed without an early return does the pass evaluate `mutated`'s final, cumulative value -- true if it was set during the bump step, during the rewrite step, or both, and this is the ONLY value the persist decision consults; a snapshot of `mutated` taken right after the bump step alone is never used to gate persist -- and call handle.persist(permit) if and only if that final value is true, exactly once, never more. Because every rewrite actually iterated in rewrite_indices without erroring sets `mutated` true, the final value is false in exactly one case: `bump` is Some and its precondition check took the skip branch (current == target_version, no write_version call) AND `rewrite_indices` is empty -- a solo bump-only group where the manifest was already at its target version and there is nothing else to write for that path. That single case matches today's zero-persist behavior for an already-at-target manifest with no other writes (see apply_is_idempotent_when_manifest_already_at_target_version, required to keep passing unmodified by AC-009, and AC-002's 'not by N' persist-count requirement). Critically, a skipped bump combined with one or more successfully-applied rewrites on the SAME path DOES reach persist -- `mutated` becomes true during the rewrite step even though the bump step alone left it false, so the rewrite's in-memory mutation is never silently dropped -- and this specific combination (bump present but skipped, at least one rewrite that does apply) has its own dedicated test; see AC-016.

api_surface.name: persist_call_count / reset_persist_call_count
api_surface.description: New functions added to crates/callisto-manifests/src/lib.rs, backed by a new process-global AtomicUsize (PERSIST_CALL_COUNT) distinct from the existing OPEN_CALL_COUNT (lib.rs:114). Each of CargoToml::persist, PackageJson::persist, and PyprojectToml::persist increments PERSIST_CALL_COUNT by one immediately after its underlying atomic_write call returns Ok -- a persist call that returns Err (e.g. the atomic_write failure path exercised by SPEC-MANIFEST-PERSIST-001's AC-011/AC-011b) does NOT increment the counter. WorkspaceCargoResolver's own persist method does not increment this counter (see non_goals) -- it is scoped exclusively to the Manifest trait's three implementors, matching the scope of the batching this spec introduces. Test-observability only; production code never reads these functions, matching open_call_count's existing doc comment convention (lib.rs:108-113).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a VersionPlan containing N (N >= 2) PlannedBump/SpecRewrite entries whose Manifest-trait-routed writes (VersionWriteTarget::Manifest / DepWriteTarget::Manifest) all target the same manifest path P, and no entry in the same plan routes a WorkspaceCargoResolver write (VersionWriteTarget::CargoWorkspacePackage or DepWriteTarget::CargoWorkspaceDependency) to root_manifest == P: calling reset_open_call_count() immediately before apply_version_plan(...), then reading open_call_count() immediately after, shows the counter increased by exactly 1, not by N. (open_call_count is a process-global counter, not per-path; since this fixture's only Manifest-trait writes in the whole plan target P, an increase of exactly 1 unambiguously reflects a single open for P.) Verified in a dedicated #[serial] integration test in crates/callisto-graph/tests/apply_persist_open_count_test.rs, following the existing T20 precedent in that file.

For the same N-entries-one-file scenario as AC-001: calling reset_persist_call_count() immediately before apply_version_plan(...), then reading persist_call_count() immediately after, shows the counter increased by exactly 1, not by N. This is verified in the same dedicated #[serial] integration test as AC-001, asserting both counters in the same test body around the same apply_version_plan call.

For a manifest fixture P receiving both one bump mutation and two or more rewrite mutations in the same batched group, calling apply_version_plan(...) and then reading P's on-disk bytes afterward shows: (a) the bumped version string is present and correct; (b) every rewritten dependency's new spec string is present and correct; (c) every part of P's original formatting NOT touched by any of the N mutations (comment placement, key ordering, indentation, quote style) is byte-for-byte identical to the pre-apply file -- verified by a new test in apply.rs's #[cfg(test)] module using a multi-entry fixture (at least one bump plus at least two rewrites on the same path), not a 1-entry byte-identity check.

For the same path P and group as AC-003, but where the bump mutation succeeds and the second of two rewrite mutations destined for P fails (e.g. targets a dependency name absent from P, producing ManifestError::DependencyNotFound): apply_version_plan returns that error, and P's on-disk bytes afterward are byte-for-byte identical to P's content before apply_version_plan was called -- neither the successful bump mutation nor the first successful rewrite mutation is persisted, because persist() for the group is never reached. This is an explicit, documented behavior CHANGE from pre-batching per-entry semantics: before this spec, entries preceding the failing one in the same file's sequence would already be on disk (each was its own immediate open/mutate/persist); after this spec, a batched group is all-or-nothing.

Given a VersionPlan where path P (a workspace root Cargo.toml) receives THREE rewrite entries in the same plan: two DepWriteTarget::Manifest(P) entries for two distinct plain, non-inherited dependency names, AND one DepWriteTarget::CargoWorkspaceDependency{root_manifest: P} entry for a third, workspace-inherited dependency name (mirroring cascade.rs's edge.inherited routing at crates/callisto-graph/src/cascade.rs ~238-247): resetting open_call_count() before apply_version_plan(...) and reading it afterward shows open_call_count() == 2 -- one open per DepWriteTarget::Manifest entry, via the unbatched per-entry pass, proving the mixed-routing exclusion correctly kept both plain-dependency entries from being folded into a single batched group. This two-plain-dependency shape is required, not optional: a fixture with only ONE DepWriteTarget::Manifest entry for P cannot discriminate a correctly-excluded path from an incorrectly-batched one, because both a working exclusion guard and a completely broken/absent one would yield open_call_count() == 1 in that case. With two plain-dependency entries, a WRONGLY-batched implementation (one that failed to detect P as mixed-routing and merged the two DepWriteTarget::Manifest entries into one ManifestWriteGroup) would instead yield open_call_count() == 1, visibly failing this assertion -- making the criterion genuinely falsifiable. Verified by a new #[serial] test in crates/callisto-graph/tests/apply_persist_open_count_test.rs.

In the AC-005 fixture, the CargoWorkspaceDependency entry's mutation (via WorkspaceCargoResolver::write_dependency against the workspace root manifest) and BOTH DepWriteTarget::Manifest entries' mutations (via the excluded path's own unbatched, per-entry Manifest-trait open/mutate/persist) all succeed independently and all land on disk after apply_version_plan returns Ok -- verified by reading the fixture's Cargo.toml bytes afterward and asserting all three new specs are present: both plain dependencies' new specs (in [dependencies]) and the workspace-inherited dependency's new spec (in [workspace.dependencies]).

classify_manifest_writes's construction of ManifestWriteClassification.excluded structurally covers VersionWriteTarget::CargoWorkspacePackage the same way it covers VersionWriteTarget::CargoWorkspacePackage's dependency-side counterpart DepWriteTarget::CargoWorkspaceDependency: verified by a unit test (calling classify_manifest_writes directly, not apply_version_plan) that hand-constructs a VersionPlan with a PlannedBump whose writes include VersionWriteTarget::CargoWorkspacePackage{root_manifest: P} alongside a SpecRewrite whose DepWriteTarget::Manifest also names P, and asserts P appears in the returned excluded set. This test exists for defensive completeness of the exclusion guard even though VersionWriteTarget::CargoWorkspacePackage currently has no production constructor anywhere in the workspace (confirmed dead code, per non_goals) -- the guard must still structurally handle it as a live, constructible enum variant.

For a VersionPlan with no mixed-routing paths and no shared-path entries at all (every Manifest-trait write targets a distinct path from every other write), running apply_version_plan and reading each modified file's on-disk bytes afterward matches the byte-for-byte assertions already proven in SPEC-MANIFEST-PERSIST-001's apply_version_plan_cargo_bump_produces_byte_identical_output_to_direct_mutate_then_persist and apply_version_plan_npm_bump_produces_byte_identical_output_to_direct_mutate_then_persist tests -- i.e. single-entry-per-file output is unaffected by the batching change.

Every test in crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs's #[cfg(test)] module that existed before this spec (including every test added by SPEC-MANIFEST-PERSIST-001: apply_persists_bumps_loop_write_version_to_disk, apply_persists_rewrites_loop_update_dependency_spec_to_disk, rewrites_loop_update_dependency_spec_error_leaves_manifest_untouched_and_skips_persist, apply_version_plan_cargo_bump_produces_byte_identical_output_to_direct_mutate_then_persist, apply_version_plan_npm_bump_produces_byte_identical_output_to_direct_mutate_then_persist, bumps_loop_write_version_error_leaves_manifest_untouched_and_skips_persist, bumps_loop_persist_failure_leaves_earlier_successful_write_intact_and_later_manifest_unchanged, rewrites_loop_persist_failure_leaves_earlier_successful_write_intact_and_later_manifest_unchanged, plus cargo_only_bump_does_not_stage_python_lockfile, refresh_lockfiles_calls_cargo_update_workspace_when_cargo_bumped, refresh_lockfiles_false_does_not_call_cargo_update, apply_is_idempotent_when_manifest_already_at_target_version, apply_returns_error_when_manifest_has_unexpected_version, apply_stages_changeset_path_even_when_file_already_deleted) continues to pass with zero modification to their test bodies after this spec's changes land, run via `cargo test -p callisto-graph`.

A dedicated unit test calls classify_manifest_writes(&plan) directly (not apply_version_plan) on a hand-constructed VersionPlan with at least three distinct manifest paths -- one receiving only a bump, one receiving only rewrites, one receiving both a bump and rewrites with no mixed routing -- and asserts the returned ManifestWriteClassification.batched map contains exactly those three paths with the expected ManifestWriteGroup contents (correct bump Option, correct rewrite_indices in plan.rewrites order), and that excluded is empty. This test requires no disk I/O and no call to apply_version_plan.

For a batched group on path P containing two SpecRewrite entries in plan.rewrites with the IDENTICAL RewriteKey (same DepWriteTarget::Manifest(P) target, same dependency name, same kind) but DIFFERENT `to` values (e.g. the first sets `helper`'s spec to "^1.1.0", the second to "^1.2.0"), a test asserts the final on-disk spec for that dependency equals the SECOND entry's `to` value, not the first -- this is only true if rewrite_indices is iterated in plan.rewrites order; an implementation that applied them in a different order (reversed, or an unspecified order derived from some internal grouping) would leave the first entry's value on disk instead, or would be nondeterministic across runs, and this assertion catches either failure. This exercises apply.rs's own #[cfg(test)] module with a hand-constructed `VersionPlan { rewrites: vec![...] }` fixture; two SpecRewrite entries sharing one RewriteKey are not producible by real cascade.rs planner output: CascadeOutcome.rewrites is declared as `BTreeMap<RewriteKey, SpecRewrite>` (crates/callisto-graph/src/cascade.rs:151), populated via `out.rewrites.insert(key.clone(), SpecRewrite { .. })` (cascade.rs:255) -- a map insert, which silently overwrites rather than duplicates on a repeated key -- and then flattened to a plain Vec via `.into_values().collect()` at both real plan-construction call sites (crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/snapshot.rs:109 and crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/version.rs:248), so no real planner-produced VersionPlan.rewrites can contain two entries with the same RewriteKey, but plan.rewrites itself is a plain Vec<SpecRewrite> with no uniqueness constraint, so this is a valid, necessary direct test of ManifestWriteGroup's own rewrite_indices iteration order, independent of whether a real plan ever exercises two same-key rewrites. This criterion deliberately does NOT attempt to prove bump-before-rewrites ordering via on-disk bytes -- see AC-017 for why that specific claim is not byte-observable and how it is established instead.

Given a VersionPlan with two distinct, non-mixed batchable manifest paths P1 and P2 whose names are chosen so that P1 sorts lexicographically before P2 as PathBuf values (e.g. P1 = "a-crate/Cargo.toml", P2 = "b-crate/Cargo.toml") -- pinning, via classify_manifest_writes's `batched: BTreeMap<PathBuf, ManifestWriteGroup>` iteration order and apply_version_plan's `?`-based short-circuit error propagation, that P1's group is fully opened, mutated, and persisted before iteration ever reaches P2's group -- where P1's batched group succeeds fully (opens, mutates, persists) and P2's batched group's persist call fails (via the same read-only-parent-directory failure injection mechanism as SPEC-MANIFEST-PERSIST-001's AC-011/AC-011b), apply_version_plan returns the propagated error (Err(GraphError::Manifest(ManifestError::Write { .. }))) and: P1's on-disk bytes reflect its already-successfully-persisted batch, unaffected by P2's later failure because P1 was processed and persisted strictly before P2 was even attempted; P2's on-disk bytes are byte-for-byte unchanged from before apply_version_plan was called (its all-or-nothing group was never persisted). This criterion depends on P1 sorting before P2 in BTreeMap order and is deliberately NOT claimed to hold under the reverse path-name assignment -- the fixture's path names pin the ordering rather than leaving it incidental, and this is a requirement on the test fixture, not an implementation detail left to the implementer's discretion.

Reading the source of crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs's WorkspaceCargoResolver::write_version and WorkspaceCargoResolver::write_dependency, and crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs's VersionWriteTarget::CargoWorkspacePackage and DepWriteTarget::CargoWorkspaceDependency match arms, after this spec's changes land shows zero modification to those four code paths compared to their SPEC-MANIFEST-PERSIST-001 state: each arm still opens/loads a fresh WorkspaceCargoResolver and calls its combined mutate+persist method immediately, once per entry, with no batching, grouping, or deferral introduced by this spec.

For a batched group on path P where P's on-disk version is already at the bump's target version (so the bump step takes the skip branch: current == target_version, handle.write_version is never called for the bump) AND the group also has one or more rewrite_indices entries that successfully apply (e.g. a dependency present in P's [dependencies] table, using the same fixture shape as AC-003 but with P pre-set to the bump's target version rather than its `from` version): apply_version_plan returns Ok; resetting persist_call_count() before the call and reading it after shows the counter increased by exactly 1, not 0 -- proving the skipped bump does not suppress the persist that the successful rewrite(s) require; and P's on-disk bytes afterward show the rewrite's new dependency spec genuinely written (not silently lost), while the version field remains unchanged at the already-correct target version. This is the one bump-precondition/rewrite-interaction combination with zero test coverage before this spec (a skipped bump combined with a successful rewrite on the same path), and is verified by a dedicated test in apply.rs's #[cfg(test)] module distinct from AC-001/AC-002 (which use a bump that actually mutates, not one that skips) and from AC-004/AC-014 (which cover failure paths, not this successful-skip-plus-successful-rewrite path).

Bump-before-rewrites sequencing within a single ManifestWriteGroup (the requirement that the bump step, if any, completes -- skip, write, or error -- strictly before any rewrite in rewrite_indices is attempted) is NOT independently provable via on-disk byte comparison for the successful-bump-then-successful-rewrite case. Verified by reading the actual mutator implementations: CargoToml::write_version (crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs:198-240) writes only [package].version (or, for a workspace-inherited member, an explicit pinned replacement of the same field); CargoToml::update_dependency_spec (crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs:288-375) writes only a dependencies/dev-dependencies/build-dependencies table entry, using `new.render()` of the DepSpec value passed in as a parameter -- a value already fully determined by the plan before apply_version_plan runs, never derived by reading the manifest's current version or any other in-memory state at apply time. These two mutators touch disjoint CST locations with values fixed independently of each other and of application order, so applying a rewrite before or after a successful bump in the same group produces byte-identical final output. No fixture -- self-referencing or otherwise -- can make this specific ordering observable in bytes, and this spec does not claim otherwise; a prior draft's 'self-referencing pin' construction does not work, because the pinned string is a plan-time constant already fixed before apply_version_plan runs, not something computed from the bump's in-memory effect at apply time. Instead, the sequencing guarantee is established jointly by AC-014 (a bump-precondition failure means no rewrite in rewrite_indices is ever attempted -- proving the bump step's precondition check runs, and is checked, strictly before the rewrite step begins) and AC-016 (a skipped bump still allows a subsequent successful rewrite to reach persist -- proving the bump step, including its skip branch, is fully evaluated before the rewrite step begins, not interleaved or reordered with it). Together, AC-014 and AC-016 falsify any implementation that runs the rewrite step before, or concurrently/interleaved with, the bump step, even though no successful-path byte assertion can do the same. AC-011 covers the separate, genuinely byte-observable claim of rewrite-to-rewrite ordering within rewrite_indices.
